features.evidence: Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, Doctoral degree
features.name: Educational attainment
features.description: Captures the highest relevant academic credential the letter presents for the role.

levels.descriptor: No degree, unrelated education, or unclear academic preparation is stated.
States a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background.
States a master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
States a doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.name: Relevant software experience length
features.description: Captures how much directly relevant professional software development time the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Less than the minimum experience is shown, or duration is not stated.
Shows roughly 2 to 3 years of relevant software experience.
Shows roughly 4 to 5 years of relevant software experience.
Shows 6 or more years of relevant software experience.

features.name: Shipped service breadth
features.description: Captures the breadth of hands-on experience across testing, maintaining, and launching production services.

levels.descriptor: No clear evidence of owning production services through launch and maintenance.
Shows limited shipped-service exposure, such as one or two services or mostly maintenance work.
Shows solid multi-service exposure across the production lifecycle.
Shows repeated ownership across many production services with clear launch and upkeep experience.

features.name: Language breadth beyond Go
features.description: Captures how much broader technical versatility the letter shows beyond the core Go requirement.

levels.descriptor: Only Go is mentioned, or language breadth is unclear.
Shows Go plus one or two additional languages.
Shows Go plus several additional languages.
Shows Go plus broad multi-language experience across many systems.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how explicitly and substantively the letter shows Python experience relevant to back-end, tooling, or automation work.

levels.descriptor: No Python experience is mentioned.
Python appears only incidentally, such as alongside agents, without much ownership detail.
Describes regular Python use for tooling, scripts, analysis, or internal automation.
Shows production-grade Python ownership, such as services, typed or tested code, or widely used internal tooling.

features.name: Applied AI production experience
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows hands-on experience building AI-enabled systems and thinking about their reliability.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Shows only general interest in AI or vague exposure.
Describes concrete shipped AI or LLM-backed features.
Describes shipped AI work together with evaluation, trustworthiness, or failure-mode handling.

features.name: Agentic system design
features.description: Captures experience designing agent-based tooling rather than merely using AI features.

levels.descriptor: No agentic tooling is mentioned.
Mentions agents or autonomous tooling vaguely, without architectural detail.
Describes building agentic tooling that pairs Python agents with Go back-end services.
Describes end-to-end agent architecture with explicit guardrails, permissions, auditing, or bounded autonomy.

features.name: Security assessment experience
features.description: Captures whether the letter demonstrates practical experience assessing systems for security risk.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Security review is mentioned briefly or abstractly, with little method detail.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, design review, or formal assessments.
Shows repeated structured assessment practice with remediation follow-through or strong attacker-minded depth.

features.name: Vulnerability workflow automation
features.description: Captures experience turning vulnerability intake or handling from manual work into tooling.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
Mentions security automation generally, but not a concrete vulnerability workflow.
Describes concrete automation of vulnerability intake, routing, triage, or deduplication.
Describes concrete vulnerability automation with clear operational impact, such as major manual-work reduction or mostly self-running handling.

features.evidence: replacing a crumbling heuristic with a clean algorithm
features.name: Algorithmic problem-solving
features.description: Captures whether the letter demonstrates data-structure and algorithm fluency through specific engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is shown.
Claims algorithmic strength without a concrete example.
Gives one concrete example of an algorithmic redesign or data-structure choice improving a system.
Gives especially strong or repeated evidence of algorithmic thinking tied to meaningful performance or correctness gains.

features.evidence: maintainer of an actively used open-source project
features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows responsibility beyond private codebases through upstream contribution or maintenance.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or one-off fixes to dependencies.
Describes regular contribution or maintenance responsibility.
Shows stewardship of an actively used project or community, including review and release responsibility.

features.name: Formal security credentialing
features.description: Captures whether the letter provides third-party validation of security knowledge or hands-on offensive skill.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a foundational security certification.
Mentions a hands-on technical security certification such as OSCP.
Mentions multiple substantial security credentials.

features.name: Offensive practice outside work
features.description: Captures the extent to which the letter shows active attacker-minded practice through competitions or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive security practice is mentioned.
Mentions occasional participation.
Describes regular participation or a sustained habit of practice.
Describes strong competitive results or unusually serious offensive practice.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the scale and technical relevance of side projects used as evidence of engineering depth.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small or lightly relevant side project.
Mentions a substantial build with meaningful systems design work.
Mentions an ambitious, technically demanding project closely relevant to backend reliability, distributed systems, or security tooling.

features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter explains why this exact security engineering role is appealing rather than a generic software job.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in the company or job title with little role-specific reasoning.
Shows some relevant interest, but the motivation remains broad or interchangeable.
Clearly ties motivation to security engineering, developer enablement, or backend tooling.
Gives nuanced and convincing motivation tightly tied to this team's charter and responsibilities.

features.evidence: scale scarce security judgment across an entire company
features.name: Leverage model understanding
features.description: Captures whether the letter understands the job as high-leverage infrastructure that multiplies security impact across many teams.

levels.descriptor: Shows no clear understanding of the team's leverage or platform role.
Mentions scale or impact only in generic terms.
Clearly frames the work as reducing toil or helping many engineers through tooling.
Articulates a sophisticated leverage model, such as scaling scarce expertise, making the secure path the easy path, or compounding impact across the lifecycle.

features.name: Security-partner orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents the candidate as ready to collaborate closely with security specialists rather than operating in isolation.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.evidence: queue went from a dreaded chore to something the tooling mostly runs itself
features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates claims with named examples, mechanisms, or outcomes.

levels.descriptor: Mostly gives abstract claims or lists qualifications with little support.
Provides some concrete examples, but effects or mechanisms remain vague.
Provides multiple concrete examples with clear tasks or effects.
Consistently backs claims with specific projects and believable operational outcomes.

features.evidence: someone always inherits what we build
features.name: Reliability mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames the candidate as someone who values operability, inheritability, and long-term maintenance.

levels.descriptor: Shows no clear maintainability or reliability orientation.
Uses generic quality language without a distinct maintenance perspective.
Explicitly emphasizes maintenance, quiet resilience, inheritability, or dependable systems.
Shows a strong maintainer philosophy grounded in experience fixing failures, operating systems, or designing for long-term stewardship.

features.evidence: software that guards other software must be built to a higher standard
features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents a memorable point of view or story rather than only a qualifications list.

levels.descriptor: Reads as a flat inventory of credentials with little voice or through-line.
Has competent framing, but feels generic or interchangeable.
Shows a clear personal perspective, thesis, or story that shapes the letter.
Uses a memorable, cohesive narrative voice that strengthens the case for fit.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the mechanical professionalism of the letter's prose, including spelling, grammar, and readability.

levels.descriptor: Frequent distracting errors or awkward phrasing undermine credibility.
Noticeable errors are present, but the letter remains understandable.
Prose is mostly clean, with only minor slips.
Writing is crisp, polished, and essentially error-free.
